title: Science Review: Testing Hypotheses and Explaining Anomalies

review_words.key_point_zh: 可数名词，复数为 hypotheses；强调“可被证据检验”，与 assumption（未经检验的假定）、theory（较系统的解释）不能随意互换。
review_words.example: Before collecting any data, the team wrote down a hypothesis that could be proved wrong.
review_words.translation_zh: 在收集任何数据之前，团队写下一个有可能被证伪的假说。
review_words.note_zh: 搭配 formulate / write down a hypothesis；定语从句说明它“可被证伪”，这正是 hypothesis 的核心特征。

review_words.meaning_zh: 以观察或实验为依据的；实证的
review_words.key_point_zh: 常与 evidence、data、research 搭配，并与 theoretical 形成对比；写作中用 empirical evidence 代替口语化的 real proof。
review_words.example: The argument rests on anecdote rather than empirical data, so it is unlikely to persuade a scientific audience.
review_words.translation_zh: 这一论点依靠的是轶事而非实证数据，因此不太可能说服科学界的读者。
review_words.note_zh: rest on A rather than B 是常见论证句式；empirical 修饰 data/evidence 时最自然。

review_words.key_point_zh: 强调“表面上合理但未必正确”，阅读推断题常据此设错；比 credible 弱，比口语化的 believable 正式。
review_words.example: At first the idea sounded plausible, but a single counter-example was enough to undermine it.
review_words.translation_zh: 起初这个想法听起来颇有道理，但仅仅一个反例就足以动摇它。
review_words.note_zh: sound / seem plausible 是高频搭配；注意 plausible 不等于“已被证实”。

review_words.key_point_zh: 科学类阅读中常指偏离规律的异常数据或现象，复数为 anomalies；比 exception 更强调“反常”。
review_words.example: The team noticed an anomaly in the results and spent a week checking whether it was a measurement error.
review_words.translation_zh: 团队在结果中发现了一个异常，并花了一周时间核查它是否是测量误差。
review_words.note_zh: 搭配 notice / explain an anomaly；其后常接 in + 数据或领域。

review_words.key_point_zh: 多修饰 research、method、testing，含“标准严格、方法严密”之意，比 thorough 更强调严格性；阅读中常被 careful、strict 同义替换。
review_words.example: Before the findings were published, the study went through a rigorous review by independent experts.
review_words.translation_zh: 在研究结果发表之前，该研究经过了独立专家的严谨评审。
review_words.note_zh: go through a rigorous review / testing 是学术语境中的常用搭配。

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Did you finish reading that paper on how city light affects birdsong?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: I did, but I'm not convinced. The hypothesis is interesting — that artificial light shifts when birds sing — but the evidence is thin.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Mostly observations from a single park. There's no empirical data from other cities, so the pattern might just be local.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Still, the explanation sounds plausible. Didn't they also mention some kind of anomaly?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Yes — one colony sang at completely different times, and they never explained why. That makes me doubt the method.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.text: Fair enough. A rigorous study would have checked that before publishing. Maybe we can still use it in our presentation as a warning about jumping to conclusions.

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.text: Agreed. It's a useful lesson in telling a plausible story apart from tested evidence.

quiz.question: Which word is closest in meaning to "plausible" in the sentence "The report offers a plausible account of the decline"?
quiz.explanation_zh: plausible 意为“看似合理、可信”，与 credible 最接近；certain 语气过强，表示确定无疑；precise 和 detailed 谈的是细节的精确与详尽，不涉及可信度。

quiz.question: There is now considerable empirical evidence ___ the link between sleep and memory.
quiz.explanation_zh: 固定搭配 evidence for sth 表示“支持某事的证据”，empirical evidence for 是学术写作中的常见组合；其余介词不与 evidence 构成这一搭配。

quiz.question: The readings from the northern station were so different from every other station that the researchers treated them as a(n) ___ and rechecked the equipment.
quiz.explanation_zh: 此处指偏离正常规律的异常数据，用 anomaly 最准确；hypothesis 是待检验的假说，assumption 是未经检验的假定，exception 指不符合规则的情况，但不强调“反常数据”。
